fragments.text: We are going to have a conversation this morning, a conversation on how artificial intelligence is assisting government or facilitating government communication, how it is enhancing it, how it is strengthening it. I'm going to direct in the Ministry of Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services, the government of Zimbabwe. So what we have noticed is that the advent of artificial intelligence has assisted in transforming the whole landscape of media and communication. And one is transformed our way of gathering the content, number two, the distribution of the content. And number three, the consumption of the content. So what it is done effectively is that it has made accessibility of information far more faster, far more efficient and far more reliable.

And what we have done with artificial intelligence is that we have been able to make sure that our data sets are accessible to people in different places, in different systems. And that has enhanced accessibility to information. But I need to say that the access to information hasn't been without challenges. There are challenges of cultural and social values that sometimes artificial intelligence doesn't respect. And that is caused a little discomfort in some of our people. But on the main, what we have seen is benefiting the people from artificial intelligence, is that number one, it is helping them access automated information. So automated information is easier in terms of each summation for people. So if you have got different data sets and you want to find information which is useful

for whatever you're looking for, you can get a summation very fast using artificial intelligence. We are also utilizing the algorithms to make sure that certain information which we feel is an important case access, the faster and better than information which would be useless. So the algorithms are coming in handy and they are helpful. We are also seeing that chat boards are helpful in that the feedback that the citizens would want to get in real time is easily given to them. So this technology of chat boards has helped people, for example, looking for bed certificates, looking for passports or driver's license and things like that, which is useful government information which the public wants to make decisions.

So through chat books, we are able to give them that information faster and without so much of human interference or human beings in the loop. But the problem is around data security. The nature of government is that some of the information which is sensitive and sometimes which is useful to the security people. So by accessing these data sets, we still are grappling with how best we can give information which is public information and leave information which is policy and administrative. So those are the few complications that we are encountering in the meantime. But the impact is great, it is ensured that we have transparency, there is accountability and that sits and get better information in real time and that there is civic engagement

and there is better and a faster way of decision making. So I would say this is how it is playing out in our landscape, in Zimbabwe, that at Fischer Intelligence it hasn't been always about bad things, it is also strengthening the practice of communication and government messaging which I am in charge of, thank you.
